| M098 | Broad command controls used strong `ICommand.CanExecuteChanged` subscriptions before `WeakCommandSubscription` | Occurred when controls assigned a long-lived custom `ICommand` whose `CanExecuteChanged` event used strong handlers. Many command-bearing MAUI elements could be retained by the command unless the command changed or the element was otherwise cleared. Fixed upstream by PR `#29837`, which introduced `WeakCommandSubscription` for core `ICommandElement` controls. Work around on affected builds by using MAUI `Command`/weak-event command implementations or clearing command properties before disposal/navigation. | Cross-platform Controls | Button/ImageButton/MenuItem/RefreshView/SearchBar/SearchHandler/TextCell command elements, custom long-lived commands, `CanExecuteChanged` handlers | Unbounded per subscribed control while the command lives on affected builds | Regular for apps using static/shared view models or reference-bound commands | [#29837](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/29837) | [#29837](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/29837) |
| M099 | Android foreground-service app relaunch kept old Windows/Window scopes alive because `Window.Destroying()` and alert cleanup did not run | Occurred when an Android app used a foreground service and the Activity was destroyed while the process stayed alive. `Window.Destroying()` was missed in the Activity destroy path and `AlertManager`/MessagingCenter roots could keep old `Window` and scoped service instances alive after relaunch. Fixed upstream by PR `#16045` and backport `#16240`, which call `Destroying()` from `OnDestroy()` and unsubscribe alert manager state during window destruction. Work around on affected builds by avoiding foreground-service process retention across Activity destruction or explicitly tearing down window/alert state. | Android | Old `Window`, scoped services, `AlertManager.AlertRequestHelper`, MessagingCenter subscriptions, Activity/window lifecycle state | Process lifetime across Activity destroy/relaunch when a service keeps the app alive | Specific to foreground-service/background lifecycle apps, but severe when triggered | [#15972](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/15972)<br>[#16045](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/16045)<br>[#16240](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/pull/16240) | [#15972](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/15972) |
| M100 | Essentials static sensor and adjacent device events retain subscribers on app-lifetime singletons | Occurs when pages or view models subscribe to static Essentials events such as `Accelerometer.ReadingChanged` and do not unsubscribe. The static facade forwards to an app-lifetime `Default` singleton whose implementation stores plain multicast delegates; `Stop()` stops platform sensor monitoring but does not clear managed event delegates. Same-shape device facades such as `Clipboard`, `DeviceDisplay`, `Geolocation`, and Android `Platform.ActivityStateChanged` were reviewed under this class unless a MAUI-owned subscriber misses cleanup. Work around by unsubscribing with `-=` in the same lifecycle path, or by wrapping app subscriptions with weak-event logic. | Cross-platform Essentials; issue repro covers Mac Catalyst, Android, and iOS, with shared facade patterns relevant to Windows/Tizen too | Sensor/connectivity/battery/device event subscribers, page/view-model graphs, captured services and payloads | Process-lifetime per forgotten subscription while the singleton lives | Regular for sensor/device pages that subscribe on appear and only call `Stop()` or equivalent cleanup on disappear | [#36216](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/36216) | [#36216](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/36216) |
| M101 | `AnimationExtensions` strands low-level tweeners in static `s_tweeners` when animations are disabled | Occurs when `IAnimationManager.Add(...)`, `IAnimationManager.Insert(...)`, or `AnimateKinetic` is used while `Ticker.SystemEnabled` is false. `AnimationExtensions` stores the `Animation` in static `s_tweeners` before `Commit()`, then `AnimationManager.Add()` returns without running the animation or firing `Finished`, so the cleanup callback never removes the entry. Work around by checking `Ticker.SystemEnabled` before low-level `Add`/`Insert`/kinetic calls or by calling `Remove(id)` explicitly. | Cross-platform animation core | `AnimationExtensions.s_tweeners`, `Animation`, step closures, kinetic callbacks, captured view/view-model payloads | Process-lifetime/static until explicit `Remove()` or process exit | Specific to low-level animation APIs or kinetic animations while OS/user settings disable animations | [#36217](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/36217) | [#36217](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/issues/36217) |
## Triage Matrix

These populated triage fields are inferred from the tracker proof, repro branch, source path, and platform notes. Treat them as a first-pass prioritization aid; exact fix risk and workaround quality should be revisited when a specific fix is designed.

Retained MiB values in this matrix are synthetic proof payloads. They demonstrate that a leak can retain realistic-sized objects, but they are not directly comparable across repros because each repro chooses payload size and iteration count to isolate a specific root. Use the MiB value as proof scale only, then prioritize by root lifetime, trigger likelihood, affected surface, native/resource pressure, and workaround quality.




Priority grades are first-pass triage urgency. GREF/JavaObject pressure and natural high-volume triggers such as scrolling, virtualization, image churn, and navigation loops intentionally raise priority; synthetic retained MiB values do not directly determine the grade.

Priority distribution: P0=0, P1=70, P2=280, P3=129, P4=2, P5=2.
